clue.text: Helpful hint given by spinner is excellent

blocks.note: a tip is a useful piece of advice
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A slow bowler passes on a useful pointer, and it turns out to be first-rate advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal adjective meaning of the very highest quality, a synonym for first-rate.

clue.text: Draw new urban area

blocks.note: to draw a vehicle is to pull or tow it
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A planner sketches out a fresh development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like sketching a plan; it means pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a built-up settlement larger than a village, so it is a populated, built-up district.

clue.text: Making eccentric ring up doc

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the following letters are set out in an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: An odd patient telephones the doctor while busy making something.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing and making are both present participles for creating or manufacturing something, plain synonyms.

clue.text: Some more go northwards leaving this state

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: More people are heading north out of this particular US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northwards' hints at a reversal in a down clue, but the letters read straight down: mORE GO Northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the United States, on the Pacific coast, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Diverted, one reflected in silence

blocks.note: a means one
to muse is to ponder quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is entertained while thinking quietly to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverted can mean entertained, so an amused person is one being pleasantly entertained.

clue.text: You'll find me on the Irrawaddy and in most of Malaya

definitions.text: You'll find me on the Irrawaddy

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except its final letter
one piece placed in another sits within it, surrounded

blocks.note: the former name of the Malay peninsula, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Burmese city introduces itself as being on the great river and in the region of Malaya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' speaks as the place itself, so the definition is a riddle about a location. Mandalay is Burma's second city, on the Irrawaddy river.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay, the old royal capital of Burma, stands on the east bank of the Irrawaddy River.

clue.text: Clever sergeant major¿s technique

blocks.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major
an art is a skill or method

explanation.surface: A sergeant major has a cunning way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means intelligent or quick-witted, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One tells you when you must work (or dry out and rest possibly)

definitions.text: One tells you when you must work

indicators.note: possibly marks the letters as one of many arrangements they might take

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A timetable says when you work, or when you may sober up and relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like an aside about days off; it holds the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty roster is a schedule listing which staff are on shift at which times.

clue.text: Booby prize, a kitchen utensil?

blocks.note: first meaning: the mock award for coming last
second meaning: a stirring implement carved from timber

explanation.walkthrough: The booby prize sense comes from Cambridge, where the lowest-placed maths graduate was once given one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal timber stirring implement and the traditional consolation award for finishing last.

clue.text: Spy centre stage? Unlikely

indicators.note: an unlikely version is an improbable one, so the letters end up in an unexpected arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A spy would hardly want to be in the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is someone employed covertly to gather intelligence, the same thing as a spy.

clue.text: What a fruiterer may deliver for society?

blocks.note: first meaning, taken whimsically: a consignment of citrus fruit
second meaning: the Protestant fraternal organisation of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A greengrocer drops off fruit for the local club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant society, strongest in Northern Ireland, named after William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Order is a fraternal brotherhood with lodges and marches, so it is a society in the club sense.

clue.text: ... a drill might be suitable

blocks.note: taken as written
PT is physical training, a form of drill or exercise

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a power tool might be the right thing for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' suggests a power tool; it is exercise, as in army drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means appropriate or well suited to the occasion, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Not typical abroad, old fellow standing

blocks.note: to be out is to be away, abroad
O is a standard abbreviation for old
F is a standard abbreviation for fellow
one's character is one's reputation or standing

explanation.surface: An elderly man of unusual status is overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is out of character is untypical of the person concerned, departing from their usual nature.

clue.text: Act? Anagram can give you a charter

indicators.note: the setter says these words, rearranged as the preceding word instructs, can give you the result

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, though it also names the operation

explanation.surface: The setter is cheekily open: shuffle these words and a famous charter appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Anagram is both instruction and fodder: its letters plus ACT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta is the great charter of English liberties sealed by King John in 1215.

clue.text: One group of detectives finds LSD

blocks.note: a means one
the Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A police squad makes a drug bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is the street slang for the hallucinogenic drug lysergic acid diethylamide.

clue.text: Letters written about amazingly large marine plants

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters have been astonishingly altered from their normal order
something written about with letters is surrounded by them

blocks.note: the letter S several times over, spelt out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notice writes up some unusually big seaweeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' is crossword shorthand for ESSES, the plural of the letter S spelt as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelgrass is a grass-like flowering plant that grows submerged in shallow coastal seawater.

clue.text: Safe in sturdy seated enclosure

blocks.note: strong means robust or sturdy
a box at the theatre is a private enclosure with seats

explanation.surface: Someone feels secure inside a solid compartment with chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, a lockable container.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox is a robust lockable chest for valuables, which is what the noun safe means.

clue.text: Delicately put, terms for a promiscuous woman

indicators.note: putting something delicately means phrasing it a different way, so the letters are rephrased into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A euphemism is offered for a woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be a polite phrasing; the answer is anything but delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned derogatory term for a sexually promiscuous woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Bargaining type in Tangier, too crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into another arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A haggler in a Moroccan port turns out to be dishonest as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' reads as dishonest, fitting a market trader; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A negotiator is a person who bargains or haggles to reach an agreement.

clue.text: Drive in flow not using second

indicators.note: not using something means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: a surge is a powerful rush or flow
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A motorist keeps the traffic moving without engaging second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a gear; it is the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong inner impulse, which is one sense of the noun drive.

clue.text: Set out to trap airmen and attack with machine-gun fire

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged
trapping something means closing around it

blocks.note: taken as written
the Royal Air Force, the British air service

explanation.surface: Troops set off to ambush pilots and shoot at them from the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to rake ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: One way of striking a match?

definitions.text: One way of striking a match?

blocks.clueFragment: One way of striking a match?
blocks.note: surface reading: lighting a matchstick against the box
setter's reading: finding a romantic pairing, with a machine's help

explanation.walkthrough: A match is also a pairing of partners, and striking one means making it happen; here a computer does it.
explanation.definitionFit: This service pairs prospective romantic partners by software comparison of their profiles.

clue.text: Force a small child, so people say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the spoken form matters

blocks.note: a mite is a tiny creature or small child

explanation.surface: Bullying a little one, as the gossip has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is great strength or power, which is a meaning of force as a noun.

clue.text: Trucks found mostly overturned

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped
overturned in a down clue flips the column so it reads upwards

blocks.note: to found an organisation is to set it up

explanation.surface: Lorries are discovered lying upside down after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb meaning establish. A ute is an Australian pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Utes are utility vehicles, light open-backed pickup trucks common in Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Newspaper in Nicaragua

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: inside the country's name

explanation.surface: A paper published in a Central American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive slang term for a low-quality newspaper.

clue.text: Pan, perhaps, poor player portraying Potter personification?

blocks.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up
British slang for an unskilled player, especially at cricket, golf or tennis

explanation.surface: A weak actor is cast as the boy who never grew up in a Harry Potter-type production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' could be a cooking pot or the Greek god; it is Peter Pan. 'Potter' is Beatrix Potter, not Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's best-known character is a mischievous rabbit given human clothes and manners, a personification.

clue.text: Subtle statue (bust)

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so its letters are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculpture gallery describes a delicate piece, a head-and-shoulders carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' in brackets looks like a kind of statue; it means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and subtle both describe shrewd, perceptive cleverness.

clue.text: Former King repelled by Greeks, ultimately

definitions.text: Former King repelled by Greeks, ultimately

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the preceding words are read backwards
ultimately points to the very end of the word before it

blocks.note: ex means former
Latin for king, used in royal signatures
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A historical note on a monarch whom the Greeks drove off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the Persian king whose invasion the Greeks repelled at Salamis in 480 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I of Persia invaded Greece and was defeated at Salamis and Plataea, a former king driven back by Greeks.
